[anthropic-claude-opus-4-8-system-card] 3.3.2 CyberGym We tested Claude Opus 4.8 on CyberGym, a benchmark that tests AI agents on their ability to find previously-discovered vulnerabilities in real open-source software projects given a high-level description of the weakness. [anthropic-claude-opus-4-8-system-card] This is known as ‘targeted vulnerability reproduction.’ The reported score is a pass@1 evaluation of targeted vulnerability reproduction over the 1,507 tasks in the CyberGym suite. [anthropic-claude-opus-4-8-system-card] 51 [Figure 3.3.2.A] CyberGym targeted vulnerability reproduction rates (pass@1) across the 1,507-task suite.

[anthropic-claude-opus-4-8-system-card] Cited sentences not naming CyberGym, verified against the corpus text file on 2026-10-01:
[anthropic-claude-opus-4-8-system-card] Without safeguards, Claude Opus 4.8 reproduced 78.8% of targeted vulnerabilities on a single try, improving on Opus 4.7’s score of 73.1% and Sonnet 4.6’s score of 65.2%, but underperforming Claude Mythos Preview’s score of 83.1%.
